correctness.rationale: A perfect matching in the induced bipartite subgraph forces equal selected side sizes. The one-per-side case is excluded by either the deleted matched edge or a concrete undominated vertex. For equal side size at least two, domination is immediate and Hall’s condition follows because a singleton loses at most its indexed neighbor while any selected A-subset of size at least two sees every selected B-vertex. Counting, minimality, and the Vandermonde total then follow. Exhaustive direct verification for 3<=n<=8 agrees on all 87,360 subsets.

value.rationale: The crown graph is a standard dense bipartite graph and already appears in paired-domination literature, but the prior same-object treatment uses only one minimum witness. The exact balance characterization upgrades that witness to a complete description of every feasible set, yields every coefficient of the paired-domination polynomial, and unexpectedly collapses upper paired domination to the minimum value. These are natural structural invariants of the same object rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
